messages:
alex: Hey, CI is red on my PR but pre-commit passes locally. rustfmt + mypy failing in CI only. Can someone poke?
ci-bot: [CI] build failed on ubuntu-latest • tests/format • commit 35fb2a1 — logs: https://ci.internal/35fb2a1/logs (exit code 2) :sad-parrot:
alex: Copying relevant bits — CI logs show rustfmt diffs and mypy type errors in files I didn't touch. Example: 
```
rustfmt: src/runtime/cache.rs: formatting differences found
mypy: src/python/redwood/serving/kv_cache.py: error: Incompatible return value type (got "None", expected "Dict[str, Any]")
```
rachel: Hmm. Did the pre-commit hooks change in the last commit? We recently bumped rustfmt and tightened mypy config in infra PR #412. Could be a hook/version mismatch.
sam: Can you run `pre-commit run --all-files` locally and paste output? CI runs the hooks in a clean checkout so environment differences show up often.
alex: Ran `pre-commit run --all-files` — everything green here. Local `rustfmt` is 1.4.37, CI shows 1.5.0 in the logs. Also `file` shows some files with CRLF line endings.
priya: Aha — CRLF can change rustfmt diffs downstream. If someone committed files from Windows, CI checkout will treat EOL differently. Check `.gitattributes` and `core.autocrlf`.
morgan: Quick triage plan: 1) try `git ls-files -z | xargs -0 file --mime` to spot CRLFs 2) run `pre-commit autoupdate` to sync hook versions 3) run CI rerun after bump or add `.gitattributes` to normalize.
alex: Running those now. Output for file check: `src/runtime/cache.rs: text/plain; charset=us-ascii` but `tools/scripts/schema.py: text/plain; charset=utf-8; CRLF`.
priya: That `schema.py` CRLF could cause mypy path differences if shebang/encoding lines change. Also check that CI installs rustfmt via rustup toolchain, different patch versions produce formatting diffs.
sam: If it's just rustfmt version, easiest stopgap is to pin rustfmt version in CI image or run `rustup component add rustfmt --toolchain stable` with the same toolchain. But we should fix line endings too.
alex: I can add a small cleanup commit that normalizes EOLs (run `git add --renormalize .`) and push — would that be okay or should we bisect first?
morgan: Try the normalize commit. If CI still fails, we bisect to the infra PR that bumped hooks. If you want, I can run a quick bisect on `infra/.pre-commit-config.yaml` to see which hook/version introduced the failure.
alex: Pushed eol-normalize commit — build queued.
ci-bot: [CI] re-run started for commit d7a9b8c — checks in progress...
priya: Also FYI, we had an accidental pre-commit autoupdate in staging branch last week that bumped mypy-strict plugin. If bisect points there, revert back to previous plugin version until teams can adapt.
sam: If the normalize fix clears rustfmt but mypy still complains in CI about types in untouched files, ask CI to dump `pip freeze` and python version. We had a mismatch with mypy pinned version before.
ci-bot: [CI] all checks green on d7a9b8c — format and typechecks passed :tada:
alex: Great — normalization fixed it. Leaving a follow-up issue to: pin formatter versions in CI, add `.gitattributes`, and add a CI check that prints tool versions on failures.
devops-bot: Created issue #1585: "CI tool/version pin + EOL normalization" and assigned to infra.
priya: Thanks for the quick triage everyone. If anything flares back up ping #eng and we can bisect further. :thumbsup:
